Or does it post-filter the ef_search candidates, which can return too few results unless the planner uses the B-tree index or iterative index scans?","rationale":"The NFR-2 latency claim and retrieval quality for context packs depend on how filtered HNSW queries actually execute.","needs_external":true,"capability":"search","queries":["pgvector HNSW filtering WHERE clause ef_search fewer results","pgvector 0.8 iterative index scans hnsw.iterative_scan","pgvector filtered search B-tree index exact scan"],"section_refs":["11","12"]},{"id":"RQ-004","criterion_id":"fitness_for_objectives","question":"Does Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server support the stated BM25 keyword fallback natively, or only ts_rank full-text ranking? Which of these are already acknowledged in Sections 26/28?","rationale":"The PDPA audit and governance objectives and FR-16 need these paths, and rule 6 requires checking the backlog before calling something missing.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["2","14","18","26","28"]},{"id":"RQ-007","criterion_id":"internal_consistency","question":"NFR-4 says the MMP is outside the critical request path. Specifically: core slot ceiling INTERNAL versus key accessibility_needs RESTRICTED (the Validator would REJECT it); orientation onboarding_progress typed WORKING (no persistence) yet expiring at orientation end; PUBLIC routed to memory_standard although the tier table lists only INTERNAL+RESTRICTED; FR-9 order classify→embed→validate versus the topic being chosen by sensitivity before classification; FR-13 'exactly one entry' versus enqueue and consumer both logging.","rationale":"Generating code from mutually contradictory rules produces defects, and Section 28 rates these components as Ready.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["10","11","17","18","23","27"]},{"id":"RQ-009","criterion_id":"internal_consistency","question":"P8 calls the write path 'Kafka' and Section 25 confirms 'Async via Kafka (Azure Event Hubs)'. Is that consistent with Section 26, which still lists Kafka vs Event Hubs as pending, and is Redis similarly confirmed and pending at the same time?","rationale":"A confirmed decision that rests on a pending item is an unresolved assumption that affects the write-path design and cost.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["3","25","26"]},{"id":"RQ-010","criterion_id":"claims_and_external_constraints","question":"Can Microsoft Entra ID issue 48-hour access tokens? Is text-embedding-3-small deployable in an Azure Singapore region for data residency?","rationale":"The write-path rationale and the separate sensitive-tier embedding deployment depend on these managed-service limits and on regional availability.","needs_external":true,"capability":"search","queries":["Azure Event Hubs Kafka quotas tiers message size partitions","Azure Event Hubs dead letter retry Kafka consumer","Azure OpenAI text-embedding-3-small region availability Southeast Asia"],"section_refs":["17","18","25","26"]},{"id":"RQ-013","criterion_id":"security_and_privacy","question":"Is the counselling hard wall (FR-5, P4) actually hard? Escalations written to standard-tier escalations/ may carry counselling content. Super Admin is described as 'Everything'.","rationale":"FR-5/NFR-5 require isolation at both the policy and the credential level, and these paths could bypass it.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["11","13","14","18","19"]},{"id":"RQ-014","criterion_id":"security_and_privacy","question":"Is serving from an agent backup after a token is REVOKED compatible with access-control intent? Is keeping the agent backup after a learner self-deletes compatible with FR-15 and with PDPA retention-limitation and consent-withdrawal obligations?","rationale":"These behaviours may break the learner-deletion requirement and the PDPA compliance objective that P7 and the audit rely on.","needs_external":true,"capability":"search","queries":["PDPA Singapore retention limitation obligation section 25","PDPA Singapore withdrawal of consent cease retention section 16","PDPC advisory guidelines AI recommendation decision systems personal data"],"section_refs":["6","13","15","20"]},{"id":"RQ-015","criterion_id":"security_and_privacy","question":"Does PDPA require the specific audit-log retention or access-request support the design implies ('Retained per PDPA requirements')? Do access/correction obligations and data-breach notification create requirements the design lacks? Is the unauthenticated Admin API (acknowledged in Section 28) a launch blocker?","rationale":"PDPA compliance is a stated objective, and audit retention and the PDPA sign-off are pending (backlog item 4).","needs_external":true,"capability":"search","queries":["PDPA Singapore access and correction obligation sections 21 22","PDPA data breach notification obligation 3 days","PDPC guide protection of personal data logging retention"],"section_refs":["17","21","26","28"]},{"id":"RQ-016","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"How does the design behave under term-start write spikes, consumer lag, retries with duplicates, out-of-order writes for one learner (no partition key is defined), Azure OpenAI embedding throttling, and Redis failure? Does the cached read path serve stale or now-forbidden data after a write or a policy change, given that policy decisions are 'not cached' but context packs are?","rationale":"NFR-1/NFR-3 and the 'rule change takes effect immediately' claim depend on correct behaviour under partial failure and concurrency.","needs_external":true,"capability":"search","queries":["Azure OpenAI embeddings rate limits tokens per minute throttling 429","Kafka partition key ordering per key idempotent consumer"],"section_refs":["16","17","18"]},{"id":"RQ-017","criterion_id":"scalability_and_failure_modes","question":"Is the agent per-learner backup store ('Full store always present for all learners' for six agents) sized, given a store technology and governed? Does degraded mode have a bounded staleness and a reconciliation path?","rationale":"FR-16 and P1 depend on a backup store that appears in neither the store architecture nor the sizing.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["12","13","14"]},{"id":"RQ-018","criterion_id":"assumptions_and_dependencies","question":"Which premises are unverified or untracked? These include SIS webhook reliability and its failure handling, Entra token behaviour, embedding model stability (re-embedding on model change), PDPA sign-off, and the Event Hubs/Redis choices. Which backlog items (Policy Engine algorithm, compaction, Auditor retention) block the launch scope, and do they contradict Section 28's claim that compaction can be deferred even though term-end compaction is part of the lifecycle?","rationale":"Several confirmed decisions and the build phases rest on items that are still pending.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["20","21","26","28","29"]},{"id":"RQ-019","criterion_id":"verifiability","question":"Can each Section 27 criterion verify its requirement? Cases to check: FR-5 tests only three agents and not the credential level or Super Admin; FR-6 uses static import checks only; FR-9 has an undefined 'enqueue time budget'; NFR-2 has no concurrency profile; NFR-10 is a projection rather than a measurement; FR-8 has no combination cases; FR-16 does not define 'conflicting'.","rationale":"Build Phase 9 is built on this matrix, so weak criteria let requirements go unverified.","needs_external":false,"capability":"none","queries":[],"section_refs":["27","29"]},{"id":"RQ-020","criterion_id":"verifiability","question":"What recognised benchmark method (for example ANN-benchmarks-style recall@k versus latency with filtered queries under concurrent load) should validate NFR-2 and retrieval quality?","rationale":"The NFR-2 acceptance criterion measures latency but not recall, which filtered HNSW can degrade.","needs_external":true,"capability":"search","queries":["filtered vector search benchmark recall latency pgvector","ANN benchmarks recall at k methodology"],"section_refs":["12","27"]},{"id":"RQ-021","criterion_id":"decision_preservation","question":"Can the likely refinements (token lifetime via refresh, filtered-query strategy, a dead-letter path, encryption of the agent backup and cache) be made while preserving the confirmed decisions (48-hour window, pgvector, HNSW parameters, async Kafka, counselling wall)? {"intent_summary":{"statement":"The document is the detailed design for the SIT Institutional Memory Platform. The platform is a governed memory infrastructure at institution level, not a per-agent memory store. It serves the AI Tutor, AI Buddy, Academic Advisory, Counselling, Career and Orientation agents for about 15,000 SIT learners. It provides a structured namespace per learner, access control applied before retrieval and backed by policy, an administrative control plane (MMP), audit trails for PDPA compliance, a strict counselling isolation wall, an asynchronous write path and a cached read path. SIT-AI-Factory-RAG is out of scope. The document is at design stage (build not started) and is intended to be detailed enough for engineers or an AI coding assistant to begin implementation. Section 28 assesses where it is and is not ready for that.","objectives":[{"ref":"P1","text":"The learner namespace is authoritative and the agent's copy is backup only.
